cards.text: The LORD speaks again to Moses, Israel's leader, and to Aaron, Moses' brother and Israel's priest. He gives them a message for all the Israelites about which land animals they may eat. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer under a stack of old takeout menus, and this is the first menu I've ever been excited to read.
The test for land animals has two parts: a split hoof, completely divided, AND it chews the cud. Both boxes checked, or it's off the list.

cards.question: True or false: a land animal that chews the cud but doesn't have a divided hoof still makes the cut.

cards.text: Then God names some animals that only get halfway there. First up is the camel, and the camel chews the cud.

cards.question: The camel chews the cud. So how does the camel do on God's two-part test?

answers.text: Unclean since its hoof isn't divided
Clean since it chews the cud
Clean but only for the priests

cards.text: Rock badger: chews the cud, no divided hoof, UNCLEAN. Rabbit: chews the cud, no divided hoof, UNCLEAN.

cards.question: The pig has a split hoof, completely divided. But it doesn't chew the ___, so it's ___.
True or false: the Israelites can't eat the camel, the rock badger, the rabbit or the pig, but touching their carcasses is no problem.

cards.text: Now God leaves dry land and heads into the water. I'll watch from up here, friend, because a stamper on a gold base doesn't swim, he SINKS.

cards.question: What does a water creature need to have for the Israelites to eat it?

cards.text: Everything in the seas or streams without fins and scales is detestable to them. God says it, and then He says it AGAIN, and when God repeats Himself, I put down my whisk and listen.

cards.question: True or false: for the detestable water creatures without fins and scales, the only rule is don't eat them.

cards.text: Then God lists the birds they must not eat: the eagle, vultures, falcons, ravens and FIVE kinds of owl, friend, I counted twice. And the last one on the bird list is the bat.
Next up: flying insects that walk on all fours. Detestable, God says, and friend, I was not about to argue.

cards.question: Flying insects that walk on all fours are detestable to Israel. But God makes an exception for the ones with jointed legs above their feet for ___ on the ground.
So which of these makes the list of insects Israel may eat?
True or false: besides the hopping kind, Israel may eat other four-legged flying insects too.

cards.text: Now God switches from eating to touching, and friend, I'm a stamper, touching is my whole JOB. These creatures will make the Israelites unclean.

cards.question: Someone touches the carcass of one of these creatures. How long is that person unclean?
True or false: if someone picks up one of these carcasses, he has to wash his clothes.

cards.text: God circles back to the land animals. Hooves not completely divided, or no chewing the cud, means unclean, and whoever touches one is unclean too.

cards.question: True or false: four-footed animals that walk on their paws are clean for Israel.

cards.text: Pick up one of those carcasses, and it's the same rule: wash your clothes, unclean until evening. Then God lists the unclean crawlers: the mole, the mouse and a whole lineup of lizards, all the way down to the chameleon, if you can even spot him.

When one of these dies and falls on something, God covers it all: wood and clothing get rinsed, a clay pot gets broken, an OVEN gets smashed, and a spring or dry seed stays clean. I had to sit down for the oven one, friend.

cards.question: An animal Israel IS allowed to eat dies. True or false: touching its carcass is no problem.

cards.text: Eat from that carcass, or pick it up, and you wash your clothes and you're unclean until evening. Then God comes back to every creature that moves along the ground: detestable, not to be eaten.

cards.question: God says not to eat creatures that move along the ground. Which ones does that cover?

answers.text: Belly crawlers and those with four or more feet
Only the ones crawling on their bellies
Only the ones with more than four feet

cards.text: Don't defile yourselves by any crawling creature, God says. And after all those camels and owls and lizards, He gives the why, and friend, I have been WAITING for this.

cards.question: God tells Israel to consecrate themselves and be holy. What reason does He give?
God reminds Israel who He is: the LORD who brought them up out of the land of ___ so that He would be their God.

cards.text: And then that line again: "be holy, because I am holy." Then God wraps it up: this is the law about animals, birds, water creatures and crawling things.

cards.question: So with this whole law about animals, what does God say Israel must be able to do?

answers.text: Tell the unclean from the clean
Offer each animal on the altar
Name each creature by its kind

cards.text: And that's where we'll stop for now, friend. God's not done teaching about clean and unclean, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: Card 2 has already answered this card. It says the test has two parts and ends "Both boxes checked, or it's off the list." Card 3 then asks whether an animal that checks only one box (chews the cud, no divided hoof) still makes the cut. That restates card 2 in the negative, so the baker reads the answer instead of working it out. Card 5 then asks the same thing again with the camel.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The setup says God names animals that "only get halfway there," then says the camel chews the cud. That rules out both "Clean" answers on card 5 before the baker picks, leaving only "Unclean since its hoof isn't divided."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says "one of these creatures," which points back to card 1. Card 1 isn't on screen anymore, so the baker doesn't know which creatures are meant.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says "one of these carcasses," which points back to card 1. Card 1 isn't on screen, so the question doesn't say which creatures it means.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The setup says God comes back to "every creature that moves along the ground." Both wrong answers on card 10 start with "Only," so the word "every" rules them out before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with "Only" and the right answer is the only one that covers everything. That pattern makes the right answer stand out from the other two.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card says that "after all those camels and owls and lizards, He gives the why." That ties the reason in Leviticus 11:44 to the whole chapter. But in the text, verses 43 and 44 attach the reason to the crawling creatures ("You must not defile yourselves by any creature that crawls along the ground"). The text leaves open whether it also covers the camels and the birds.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
